text:
Lena (People Ops): sharing a compact pack for two things managers asked for: 1) short phrasing to give upward feedback (IC -> manager) during reviews, and 2) coachable self-review prompts that encourage career signals. keep it safe and constructive.

Lena (People Ops): UPWARD FEEDBACK LINES (ICs can paste these into self-reviews or say in 1:1s)
- Positive: "Manager highlight: helped unblock hiring for our infra work; regular check-ins kept the rollout smooth."
- Request: "Ask: more visibility into roadmap prioritization, e.g., include us in the weekly planning sync or share a short note on tradeoffs."
- Constructive: "Opportunity: would value clearer expectations on deployment ownership; a short checklist before rollouts would help."
- Tone-safe miss: "Challenge: timing misalignment on priorities impacted delivery; proposed a weekly priority sync as mitigation."

Lena (People Ops): MANAGER-FACING COACH PROMPTS (use to help directs craft self-reviews)
- Growth focus (1 line): "Name one skill you want to stretch next cycle and one activity that would help (project, pairing, course)."
- Impact focus (1-2 bullets): "List top outcome + metric, then one thing that blocked faster progress."
- Collaboration focus (1 line): "Name one cross-team partner and the result you achieved together."
- Career signal (1 line): "Share one example where you coached or mentored someone, and one next step to expand that influence."

Omar (Eng Manager): these are great. can you add a tiny "how-to" for giving upward feedback without burning bridges?

Lena (People Ops): sure -> UPWARD FEEDBACK HOW-TO (3 bullets)
- Start with evidence: lead with a concrete example, not a personality note. e.g., "When we missed the rollout window (date), we lacked a rollback doc."
- Offer a solution: pair the issue with a proposed fix. e.g., "Suggest: 15m checklist + on-call owner for rollouts."
- Close with impact: explain why it matters. e.g., "This will reduce post-release incidents and speed recovery."

Kai (IC): can we have a neutral phrase for "missed goals" that shows learning and avoids absolutes?

Lena (People Ops): MISSED GOAL NEUTRAL LINE (paste)
- "Goal not met due to X (owner: team Y); shipped mitigation A and scheduled follow-up to finish remaining work by <date>. Key lesson: <one-sentence lesson>."

Lena (People Ops): PERFORMANCE CONVERSATION AGENDA (20m) - manager copy/paste
- 0-3m: confirm the employee's 2-3 bullets (outcomes + blocker).
- 3-8m: manager highlight with evidence link (PR/metric/dash).
- 8-13m: discuss one blocker and agree owner + timeline.
- 13-17m: career stretch & manager support (one ask).
- 17-20m: agree on 2 next actions and a check-in date.

Rhea (Recruiter): please include a hiring-signal line managers can paste into notes; helps prioritization.

Lena (People Ops): HIRING SIGNAL TEMPLATE (one line)
- "Hiring suggestion (priority: high/med/low): role: <title>; reason: <one-line rationale & impact>."

Frank (People Ops Bot): Reminder: paste self-review 48h before meeting (scheduled 1825170000).

Omar (Eng Manager): small suggestion: ask ICs to link one artifact (PR, dashboard) to make calibration faster.

Lena (People Ops): added a CHECKLIST FOR ICs (one-line paste)
- "I added 2 bullets + 1 artifact link (PR/metric) and one manager ask."

Kai (IC): thanks. last ask: can you add a simple DEI-aware phrase so feedback doesn't penalize different communication styles?

Lena (People Ops): DEI-AWARE FEEDBACK TIP (one line)
- "Focus on observable behaviors and outcomes (what happened, impact), avoid interpretations about intent."

Rhea (Recruiter): perfect. i'll surface the hiring lines with priority tags in our weekly headcount sync.

Omar (Eng Manager): copying these into my review calendar invites now. short and usable ":thumbsup:"

Lena (People Ops): gratitude! ping #people-ops if you want role-specific variants (SRE, ML, Product) and i'll drop them.
